claims.claim: A paper-book library loan normally ends on its agreed due date or when the borrower returns the book early.
After a borrowed paper book is returned, it normally remains in the library’s collection and is available for another reader.
The publisher’s withdrawal of the ebook caused the reader’s access to end during the active library loan.
The publisher was outside the library-loan transaction through which the reader received access.
Public libraries generally provide ebook access through licenses rather than ownership-based lending arrangements.
Publishers and ebook platforms generally set the terms governing libraries’ licensed ebook access.
A library ebook’s Borrow button generally operates through publisher- and platform-controlled licensing systems.
The seller of the ebook arrangement retained the power to revoke an active library loan remotely.
That seller exercised its revocation power against both the library and the reader in this incident.
Readers are increasingly accessing cultural works through digital systems.
The digital systems through which readers access cultural works can change access terms after access has begun.
